messages:
maya: Heads-up: we're seeing a sudden 4-6x P99 token latency in na-west gpu pools. Started ~22:12 UTC. KV cache miss rate jumped and rebalancer logs show a flurry of pod restarts. Not sure if it's networking or runtime regression.

ops-bot: ALERT: high_inference_latency detected on cluster na-west-gpu-pool (p99 > 1.8s) — incident created: INC-6781

ashwin: On it. Can someone paste the SRE dashboard? I want to confirm whether it's node-level (NIC errors) or application-level (batcher/kvcache).

sam: Dashboard: https://grafana/reports/na-west/infra-latency — p50 stable, p95 up 2x, p99 spike. NIC drops show small burst at 22:11 but not sustained.

claire: Logs from rebalancer show repeated eviction loops: "failed to attach volume" followed by "evicting pod for allocation" — maybe underlying NVMe flapping?

maya: Also saw an uptick in large batches being formed; batcher logs show many requests hitting the slow path (kv-cache cold miss). Could be a runtime change in newest image. We pushed runtime:v2.14 yesterday to canaries.

ashwin: Do we have a quick way to test runtime v2.13 vs v2.14 on a canary instance? If v2.14 regressed KV cache behavior, that would explain misses.

sam: I can spin a small test pool with v2.13 and replay a sampled traffic trace. Give me 5 min.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started job replay-trace-178345 (user: sam)

claire: Meanwhile, network ops — if this is NVMe or NIC interrupts, we should consider cordoning affected nodes and shifting traffic. Costly but keeps latency down.

maya: Prioritize quickly: 1) verify runtime regression 2) if confirmed, rollback v2.14 in na-west 3) temporary traffic shift to na-east/dedicated spare capacity if rollback not immediate.

sam: Replay results: v2.13 P99 ~ 240ms, v2.14 P99 ~ 1.9s with identical trace. KV cache miss rate in v2.14 is 18% vs 3% in v2.13. Reproducible locally.

ashwin: OK that's the smoking gun. What changed in v2.14? I see a batching heuristic tweak and a small refactor of KV cache admission. I will roll that back in a patch and push v2.14.1 ASAP.

maya: Rollback plan: set runtime image back to v2.13 on na-west via canary -> 30% -> 100%. Do we have capacity to absorb traffic during canary?

claire: We have some reserved hotpools in na-east and dedicated pools with spare headroom ~15%. We can shift lower-priority customers first. If we need to, we can enable emergency burst to dedicated with autoscale override.

ashwin: I'll prepare the rollback patch and test. ETA ~15m.

ops-bot: infra-bot: initiated traffic-shift plan SHIFT-231 to move 10% of na-west traffic to na-east using routing policy 'latency-fallback' — requires ack from eng-infra leads.

maya: Ack. Start shifting 10% now and monitor errors/latency.

sam: Shift started. First 10% shows latency stable for shifted traffic. na-west still bad but load reduced by ~9%. KV miss rate decreased marginally.

claire: I'm cordoning 3 nodes showing NVMe errors to isolate possible hardware noise. Draining pods off them now.

ashwin: Patch ready, running unit + integration tests on canary image v2.14.1. If green, we can rollout quick rollback to v2.13 or reintroduce KV admission fix in v2.14.1.

maya: If rollback takes too long, prepare an emergency config to reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 (quick config flip) to avoid slow-path batching until patch/rollback. That reduces throughput but should cut tail latency.

sam: Applying batch size cap on live routing (route config) across na-west canaries.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: applied route override batch.cap=32 to service inference/na-west (user: sam)

sam: After batch cap, p99 for na-west dropped from 1.9s -> 700ms. Not ideal but acceptable while we finish rollback.

ashwin: v2.14.1 canary tests passed. Rolling back to v2.13 now via automated rollout (canary->100%).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout to na-west runtime:image=v2.13 (initiator: ashwin)

claire: Nodes drained / cordoned cleared NVMe errors on 2/3, third still in progress. Storage vendor alerted for the remaining node.

maya: Monitor per-tenant errors — ensure no data-plane auth regressions while rolling image. Also watch cost since traffic shifted to dedicated/na-east. We should estimate incremental cost.

sam: Early metrics: after full rollback, p99 back to ~260ms, KV miss rate down to 4%. Traffic shift undone. Storage node replacement scheduled.

ashwin: Root cause: introduced a subtle race in v2.14's KV admission that caused cache entries to be evicted on certain eviction-mark races -> higher miss rate and larger batches forming. Patch in v2.14.1 fixed it but we rolled back to stable 2.13 on prod. Will include more unit tests.

maya: Postmortem items: 1) add KV admission unit/regression test harness 2) make batch-size cap easier toggle per-region 3) improve canary sampling to include tail-latency tests 4) better hardware telemetry alerts for NVMe flaps.

claire: I'll take hardware telemetry item and coordinate with vendor.

ops-bot: INCIDENT INC-6781 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Created PM: PM-989 (owner: ashwin).

maya: Great work. Let's keep monitoring for next 24h and notify if any regressions. :thumbsup:
